model_output.verdict: A youth workforce program manager with a clear progression, but little sense of the program’s reach.
write_up: You’ve moved from tutoring at City Year Baltimore to coordinating and managing youth workforce programs at Harbor Pathways. A recruiter can follow that progression and see the work, but has to guess how many students and employers your program reaches.

The grant-reporting line is a useful model: it names both the deliverable and the funders who receive it. Your current role and promotion are easy to find, and Experience is in the right place above Education.

Start with the summer jobs program, then add what your team handles and how many employer partners you recruit and onboard. Those details will give a recruiter a better sense of the program you manage without turning every line into a list of numbers.

cards.line: - Manage a summer jobs program placing high school students with local employers
cards.cannot_tell: A recruiter can see what the program does, but not how many students it serves. That number would show how much of the placement work you manage.
cards.example: Manage a summer jobs program placing [number] high school students with local employers in [period]
cards.question: How many high school students does the program place, and over what period?

cards.line: - Supervise 4 program coordinators and 20 seasonal staff

cards.example: Supervise 4 program coordinators and 20 seasonal staff who [work handled]
cards.question: What work do the coordinators and seasonal staff handle?

cards.question: How many employer partners do you recruit and onboard, and over what period?

fit.note: Your experience points toward youth workforce program management. Your progression at Harbor Pathways and supervision of coordinators and seasonal staff support that direction.
